_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — source-secret-lockdown (ocon#147). SECURITY FIX. The `source` schema had NO `authorization` block at all, so it fell back to OpenRegister's default: readable by ANY authenticated user. Combined with the fact that OR has no field-level redaction (or#380), that meant `GET /apps/openregister/api/objects/openconnector/source` returned every Source's `apikey`, `secret`, `password` and `jwt` in CLEARTEXT to any account on the instance. Verified 2026-07-13 by reading them as a brand-new user in zero groups. SourcesController's redaction is real but only guards its own endpoint — the generic OR object API reads the same rows and bypasses it entirely. On a municipality install the Sources table is where the BRP/HaalCentraal keys, ZGW credentials and SMS-gateway tokens live. Sources are ADMIN-OWNED CONFIGURATION: an operator configures them, and the sync engine — not the end user — consumes them. So every verb is admin-only. The engine keeps working for non-admin-triggered synchronisations because its own reads are switched to system context (`_rbac: false`) in the same change: it is the engine, not the user, that needs the source, and the user must never see it. This closes the disclosure; removing the plaintext credential fields entirely (so a field that cannot hold a secret cannot leak one) is the follow-up.
